title: Developer Experience: SDK Quickstarts, API Examples, and Canonical Fixes (Playbook)
author: Ethan Chen
content:
Overview:

This playbook documents the canonical approach for developer experience (DevEx) artifacts used by Redwood engineers and partner integrators: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with their canonical fixes. The goal is a consistent, high-quality surface for self-serve onboarding, lower support load, and faster iteration on SDKs and docs.

Audience:
- Developer experience engineers and technical writers
- SDK maintainers and sample-app owners
- Solutions engineers and support on-call
- Product/Platform engineers publishing docs or samples

Principles (short):
- Consistency: every quickstart follows the same UX and file layout.
- Minimal friction: getting started should take under 10 minutes with default credentials/credits.
- Reproducible: examples must be pinned to SDK versions and CI-validated.
- Observable: include diagnostics and common troubleshooting steps directly in examples.

1) SDK Guides: structure and checklist
- Recommended sections for every SDK guide:
  1) Quick summary and recommended use cases
  2) Installation (package name + pinned version)
  3) Simple example (one-liner + 5–10 line snippet that actually runs)
  4) Auth/credentials and environment variables
  5) Configuration options and performance knobs (batching, streaming, retry policy)
  6) Error handling patterns and idempotency guidance
  7) Troubleshooting and common support issues
  8) Links to quickstarts, API reference, and changelog
- SDK guide checklist (to include in PR template):
  - [ ] Example runs in CI (unit + integration smoke)
  - [ ] README has installation with exact semver
  - [ ] Auth instructions for Hosted/Dedicated/Private paths
  - [ ] Linter and formatting OK (prettier/black/ruff/eslint)
  - [ ] Docs tests: snippet runner verifies output shape

2) Quickstarts & templates: repository layout and conventions
- Canonical quickstart layout (files expected):
  - README.md: purpose, expected time-to-run, costs/credits note
  - .env.example: keys and minimal env variables
  - src/: minimal app (serverless or web client)
  - tests/: smoke test that runs the sample end-to-end with mocks or short-lived credentials
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml: build + snippet-run job
- Naming convention: short-dashed names (e.g., chat-quickstart-nodejs, embeddings-search-python)
- Template variants to maintain:
  - nodejs-rest (Express/Fetch streaming example)
  - python-fastapi (sync + async examples)
  - rust/wasm (embedding & rerank minimal)
  - terraform + k8s manifest for private deployment sample

Quickstart creation procedure (step-by-step):
1) Fork the quickstart template repo and choose template variant.
2) Implement minimal working example using the SDK's recommended patterns.
3) Add .env.example and clear cost warnings in README.
4) Add a smoke test in tests/ that uses local-mock or ephemeral sandbox credentials.
5) Open PR targeting docs-team-reviewed branch and include the PR checklist (see SDK guide checklist).
6) Assign reviewer from DevEx + one SDK owner. Merge after CI passes.
7) Tag release and add the quickstart to docs site navigation (see Docs-site procedures).

3) API examples: canonical snippets and best practices
- Goals for API examples:
  - Short (<= 15 lines) to show intent; fuller examples live as quickstarts.
  - Include both sync and streaming variants where applicable.
  - Always use realistic prompt/context and show expected shape of response.
  - Pin model and SDK versions in snippet comments.

Example — Node.js (Generation, streaming):
```js
// Requires: @redwood/sdk v2.4.1, Node 18+
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'rw-large-1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the benefits of Redwood Inference in one paragraph.' }] });
for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk); }
```

Example — Python (Embeddings + search):
```py
# Requires: redwood-sdk==2.4.1
from redwood import RedwoodClient
rc = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
emb = rc.embeddings.create(model='rw-embed-1', input=['Hello world'])
# store emb[0]['vector'] in your vector DB and run nearest neighbor queries
```

4) Docs-site operating procedures (publish flow, nav, and automation)
- High-level publish flow for docs changes:
  1) Author creates PR against docs repo; include 'docs: <short summary>' in title.
  2) Ensure snippets are runnable via snippet-runner matrix job in CI.
  3) Tag reviewers: DevEx writer + SDK owner + security if auth changes.
  4) Automated preflight: link-checker, spellcheck, accessibility lint.
  5) Merge and wait for site-build job to deploy to staging.
  6) QA on staging (smoke examples + navigation sanity).
  7) Promote to production with scheduled deploy window (default: daily 02:00 UTC).
- Navigation & taxonomy rules:
  - Keep quickstarts under /quickstarts; SDK guides under /sdk/<language>; API examples under /api-examples.
  - Short, human-first titles and a single-sentence descriptor for nav items.
  - Keep a single source-of-truth index page that lists all quickstarts by language and use-case.
- Automation tips:
  - Use snippet-runner to extract and run code blocks from markdown.
  - Use a docs-bot to automatically create PRs to update SDK versions across examples when a new release is published.

Publishing checklist (for release engineer or author):
- [ ] CI green (snippet-runner + build)
- [ ] Link-checker green
- [ ] PR has reviewers and approvals
- [ ] Staging QA done and signed off
- [ ] Update docs-site changelog entry

5) Top support issues and canonical fixes (owner + JIRA template)
- Issue: Auth failures — "invalid_api_key" or 401s
Root cause(s): expired key, wrong env var, using hosted creds against Private endpoint
Canonical fix: Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY, update .env.example with correct variable names, add guard in SDK to return actionable message ("Key appears to be from Hosted — use PRIVATE_API_KEY for private deployments").
Owner: SDK team
JIRA template summary: "Support: 401s from <LANGUAGE SDK> sample"

- Issue: Slow streaming or socket timeouts in Node quickstart
Root cause: client using long-poll vs true SSE/websocket streaming; intermediary proxies (corporate) closing idle connections
Canonical fix: Provide fallback to chunked polling with smaller chunks in quickstart, document proxy timeout workaround, add retry/backoff example in SDK docs
Owner: DevEx + Runtime networking

- Issue: Mismatched response shapes after runtime upgrade (model output changes)
Root cause: model variant switched without sample update or response parsing assumptions changed
Canonical fix: Pin model versions in examples, add eval harness smoke test verifying expected keys/fields, add opt-in leniency flag in parsing examples
Owner: Applied ML & SDK teams

- Issue: High token usage in sample prompts (customers hit surprise cost)
Root cause: long default prompt + no truncation guidance
Canonical fix: Update quickstarts with cost callouts, provide snippet that estimates token usage (pseudo-code), recommend max_tokens and token budgeting in SDK guide
Owner: DevEx + Product Pricing

Canonical fix template (to include in every support ticket/PR):
- Symptom: short free-form description
- Reproduction steps: minimal snippet + environment
- Root cause: brief technical cause
- Fix applied: code diff or README change
- Tests added: unit/integration + snippet-runner verification
- Release notes entry: yes/no

6) CI / QA guardrails for DevEx content
- Mandatory CI jobs for any docs/quickstart PR:
  - snippet-runner: extracts code blocks and runs them in sandboxed matrix
  - link-checker: external and internal links
  - spellcheck & grammar (dictionary for product names allowed)
  - license-check for third-party snippets
- Acceptance criteria for merge:
  - All CI jobs green
  - At least one SDK-owner approval

7) Troubleshooting & diagnostics to include in all quickstarts
- How to enable verbose logging in SDK (env REDWOOD_SDK_LOG_LEVEL=debug)
- How to collect request/response IDs for SRE: include header X-Request-ID and instructions to reproduce with that header
- Minimal packet of logs to attach to support ticket: snippet, env (redact keys), full error stack, request-id

Appendix: Example CLI commands and templates
- Create a new quickstart from template (CLI):
  ```bash
  npx redwood-devex create-quickstart --template=nodejs-rest --name=chat-quickstart-nodejs
  cd chat-quickstart-nodejs
  cp ../templates/.env.example .env
  # update .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY and run tests
  npm ci && npm test
  ```
- Docs publish (author):
  ```bash
  git checkout -b docs/quickstart-chat-<your-name>
  # update markdown and examples
  git commit -am "docs: add chat quickstart (nodejs)"
  git push origin HEAD
  # open PR and request devex+sdk owner reviews
  ```
